description:
## Goal

Use the deferred listener harness to prove the ordering cited by the original review: the live StrictMode setup completes before stale setup 1's listener promises resolve.

**Triage:** ready-for-agent

## Background

`src/App.tsx:182` declares `disposed` inside the lifecycle callback. StrictMode invokes that callback twice, creating different variables: cleanup 1 sets only `disposed_1`, while setup 2 owns `disposed_2`. The review claimed that if run 2 finishes first and run 1 finishes later, both listener sets could persist or startup could be skipped. That would require the runs to share one binding; they do not.

The listener lifecycle is `src/App.tsx:181-274`. Transition and refresh are registered sequentially at `src/App.tsx:192-216`; post-await checks remove stale handles; the outer check suppresses stale startup.

This task assumes the controlled harness from the preceding child exists in the focused App StrictMode test suite.

## Work

Render the real App under `React.StrictMode` with startup Issue/TauRPC calls mocked. Resolve listener promises in live-first order:

```text
T2 → R2 → T1 → R1
```

Assert at the moment `R2` settles:

- `T2` and `R2` are retained;
- the initial Issue load and `workspace_state()` each dispatch once.

Then resolve `T1` and `R1`. Assert:

- each stale unlisten spy runs exactly once immediately after its handle arrives;
- stale completion does not remove `T2` or `R2`;
- stale completion does not dispatch another startup load;
- total startup Issue and Workspace read counts remain exactly one after all microtasks flush.

Name the test so failure output identifies “live registration completes before stale registration.”

## Guardrails

- Do not change production `disposed` ownership.
- Do not replace the local flag with `useRef<boolean>`; that would make stale run 1 observe setup 2's reset value.
- Do not rely only on `applyWorkspaceTransition` or refresh revision deduplication. Assert listener/unlistener ownership directly.
- Do not use sleeps or fake timing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The live-first ordering is deterministic.
- [ ] `T2`/`R2` remain active while App is mounted.
- [ ] Late `T1`/`R1` each unlisten exactly once.
- [ ] Late stale completion cannot remove live listeners.
- [ ] Startup Issue and Workspace reads each remain at exactly one call.
- [ ] Focused App lifecycle tests and `pnpm check` pass.
title: Test live-first App listener registration under StrictMode
